Explore East Campus

East Campus

Resources, student spaces, green spaces, and athletic spaces that support environmental wellness. Use “Show on map” on any card to find it above.

Georgia Tech’s East Campus includes freshman residential halls, apartments, all fraternities and sororities, dining halls (Brittain and North Avenue), shared student spaces, pedestrian walkways, and landscaped green spaces. Compared to West Campus, East is known to be livelier and more involved in student life, mainly because of the Greek Sector and its proximity to Bobby Dodd Stadium. The Downtown Connector and its central location allow for high walkability and easy access to Tech Square and academic buildings in Central Campus. The majority of dorms in the Freshman Experience are located on East Campus, resulting in a highly social environment for first-years. The facilities and resources on campus maintain environmental wellness by supporting health, personal well-being, and sustainability, which benefits students’ social, physical, and emotional wellness.

The green spaces on East Campus impact outdoor wellness, can be used for social events, and improve one’s physical and mental health. East’s athletic spaces contribute to environmental wellness by maintaining health and personal well-being. Other shared student spaces can benefit personal well-being by molding your living environment to benefit you. Spaces that promote sustainability protect personal health and the larger Georgia Tech campus environment.

Explore West Campus

West Campus

West Campus offers residential communities, recreation, green space, focused study environments, music, dining, and wellness resources. Select “Show on map” to find a place.

West Campus is often quieter than East Campus while still offering many ways to connect with friends, build healthy habits, study, and enjoy outdoor spaces. Resources include the West Village Dining Commons (Willage), Campus Recreation Center (CRC), School of Music, Couch Park, Leadership Challenge Course, Stamps Health Services, and Eco-Commons.

These environments can support environmental wellness through movement, relaxation, focused work, and community. Some facilities or activities may require reservations or have specific access rules; check official Georgia Tech information before visiting.

Wellness Library

Environmental Wellness.

Environmental wellness can mean different things to different people. Here it is broken into three spheres, sustainability, health, and personal wellbeing, with the focus on how you can sculpt your environment, indoors and out, to best support you at Georgia Tech.

Understand the Idea

What is environmental wellness?

It means something different to everyone. To some it is cleanliness and safety, to others it is taking care of the planet. Tap a sphere to explore each meaning.

Try It

How do the spheres interact?

One small habit can touch all three spheres at once. Flip the switch to recycle a plastic water bottle and watch the effects spread.

Sustainability

The connection is the most obvious one: recycling keeps plastic in use instead of in the trash.

Health

A bottle that is not left sitting around decreases the chances for mold growth in your space.

Personal Wellbeing

A more comfortable, decluttered space is easier to relax and focus in.

Flip the switch to see the ripple effect.

Indoor Wellness

Shape your living space

Indoor environmental wellness is in essence how you keep your living spaces: how you decorate, how much light is in the room, how clean your areas are, and more. Indoor spaces are special because they are easy to modify to fit your personal preferences.

Tip: You do not need to do everything. Pick the two or three habits that fit your room and your routine, then build from there. Your checks are saved on this device.

Outdoor Wellness

Get outside, on campus and off

Outdoor wellness is in large part about the importance of time in nature. Research has confirmed that time in greenspace has cognitive, emotional, and even social benefits.

Ways to impact your outdoor wellness

The Pi Mile Walk

Go on a walk, especially if it is for pi miles. That is about 3.14 miles. Choose a pace to see how long it could take you.
